### Section 10: Long-term trajectory (Phase 3)

- Debt: (1) the floor sign's orientation (Section 11, UI-5); (2) soft shadows at maximum zoom (P-1); (3) two Mac-only baselines to keep current; (4) `fake.ts` stays as the dev and mock implementation of `SceneSignals` after chunks 18 and 22, so it must keep passing its tests; (5) the R3F 10 migration named in ADR 0001 is unchanged by this phase.
- Path dependency: the 12-slot grid positions are permanent once halls are placed (D8 "never move"); changing the grid later moves every hall. The vertex-coloured shared body ties hall looks to attribute writes, which chunks 18, 20 and 22 now assume (W-RW22).
- Reversibility: `SceneSignals` seam 5/5; per-hall colour attributes 4/5; clip-plane cutaway 4/5; campus layout grid 3/5; C25 home meaning 4/5.

### Answered decision C29 (WQ8)

Answer: A, "Add to TODOS.md (recommended)", 2026-10-14.

Commitment comparison:

| Commitment | Source/approval or pending | Current | A | B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shadow camera in Phase 3 | W-RW1 (required) | fitted to the campus extent | unchanged | unchanged |
| View-fitted shadows | none (Section 7 P-1) | none | TODOS.md P3: fit the shadow camera to the visible ground area each time the camera moves, snapped to texel steps to avoid shimmer; trigger: chunk 36 or visible blocky shadows at close zoom | none; recorded in NOT in scope |
| Chunk 36 scope | chunk 36 (approved) | quality tiers | unchanged | unchanged |

Question: D8 — C29: Should "shadows fitted to the visible area" go on the TODO list for later? Project: Synapse Horizon, branch phase-3-world-building, CEO review of Phase 3. ELI10: The campus uses one shadow picture stretched over the whole site. Zoomed out it looks fine; zoomed all the way in, each shadow pixel is about 7 screen pixels wide, so shadow edges look soft or blocky. Fitting the shadow picture to only what is on screen keeps them crisp, at some extra complexity (it must move without shimmering). Nothing approved needs it now. Stakes if we pick wrong: either a known look gap is forgotten, or the TODO list collects work nobody will do. Recommendation: A because it is a real, measurable look gap at close zoom with a natural owner (chunk 36 quality work), and writing it down costs nothing. Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score. Net: A remembers it for chunk 36; B drops it.
Header: Shadow TODO
A) Add to TODOS.md (recommended)
P3 item: view-fitted, texel-snapped shadow camera; trigger chunk 36 or visible blockiness at close zoom. Effort S, zero work now. ✅ The close-zoom shadow gap is written down with a trigger and a place to start. ✅ Chunk 36 sees it beside the other quality knobs. ❌ One more P3 item on a list that already has three.
B) Skip
Record it in NOT in scope as not worth doing; no TODO. Effort S, zero work. ✅ Keeps the TODO list to items with a clear payoff. ✅ Fixed campus-fit shadows stay simple and never shimmer. ❌ The gap is easy to forget if close-zoom shadows ever bother you.

```text

Findings, most severe first:
- E-A1 [P1] (confidence: 9/10) `src/scene/loop/driver.ts:101-104` — `if (hasRendered && !freeze) { sceneSeconds += ... }`: scene time stays 0 in every frozen shot, so emission-based vapour and packets would be empty or clumped in the C28 baseline. Resolved by E26 (D2).
- E-A2 [P3] (confidence: 7/10) `src/app/App.tsx:38` — `window.__sceneReady = value;`: W-RW29 makes ready wait for the atlas as well as the first frame; the WebGL-unavailable path still ends the loader on `unavailable` (S-RW19), so the card never waits on fonts. Recorded; no change needed.
- Production failure per new path: atlas font load fails (fallback, W-RW29); `mergeGeometries` null (W-RW13); shader patch or custom shader fails (W-RW30); route or waypoint missing (static, C23). All handled in the CEO Section 2 map.

Dispositions: E-A1 accepted (D2, E26); E-A2 no change.

### Decision ledger (eng, Phase 3)

#### E26: Particle and packet state model
Finding: E-A1, [P1], confidence 9/10, `src/scene/loop/driver.ts:101-104` (`if (hasRendered && !freeze) { sceneSeconds += ... }`, so scene time stays 0 under `freeze=1`) with docs/PLAN.md:565 (vapour "grow from 1.2 to 2.4 units over a 6 s life") and C28; reviewer Claude.
Plan baseline: W-RW7 and W-RW16 (approved): every moving value comes from `fake.ts` as a function of scene time and `seed`, frozen under `freeze=1`; WD9 (design D14) vapour values; WD8 (design D13) packet values. The state model is unspecified.
Runtime evidence: scene time is 0 for every frozen shot and baseline (driver code above). A particle system that starts emitting at scene time 0 has no vapour at 0, and packets launched at 0 sit bunched at line starts, so the C28 hero baseline and the `view=cooling` and `view=power` shots would show neither. No Phase 3 code exists yet.
Comparison grid:

| Choice | Current | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E26 particle and packet state | unspecified; emission from scene time 0 leaves frozen shots empty | closed form of time and seed: vapour particle i has age (t + offset_i) mod 6 s and shows when i < 60 x duty; packet j has phase (2.5 t + 1.2 j) mod line length for j below the rate cap | simulated per frame, pre-rolled one 6 s lifetime at start and before every frozen render | unchanged |
| Duty or rate ramp | unspecified | an index switches on or off at its next birth, so a ramp lags up to one 6 s life | new particles follow the new rate at once | unspecified |
| Determinism (W-RW7, W-RW16, approved) | required | met by construction | met with a fixed pre-roll step | not met for hero content at scene time 0 |
| WD8, WD9 values (approved) | approved | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |
| E27 opacity mechanism | pending | pending | pending | pending |
| E28 triangle budgets | pending | pending | pending | pending |

Question D2:
D2 — E26: How should vapour particles and packets keep their state, so frozen shots show them? Project: Synapse Horizon, branch phase-3-world-building, eng review of Phase 3. ELI10: Every screenshot and the campus baseline are taken with scene time frozen at 0 (driver.ts:101-104). A normal particle system starts empty and emits over time, so at time 0 the towers have no vapour and packets are bunched at the start of each line. The approved plan wants the hero to look like the mockup, with plumes and flowing packets, and every value to be a pure function of time and seed. Stakes if we pick wrong: the README hero and baselines show dead towers and clumped packets, or the simulation is harder to make repeatable. Recommendation: A because a closed-form state is full at any time, repeatable by construction and allocates nothing per frame, which matches the engineering preference for explicit over clever. Completeness: A=9/10, B=8/10, C=3/10. Net: A is simplest and always full; B allows richer motion at the cost of a pre-roll; C leaves the hero empty.
Header: Particle state
Options:
A) Closed form in time (recommended)
Vapour particle i has age (t + offset_i) mod 6 s and shows when i < 60 x duty; packet j has phase (2.5 t + 1.2 j) mod line length; seeded offsets. Effort S (human ~2h / CC ~10 min), risk low, nothing to maintain per frame. ✅ Full plumes and spread packets at scene time 0, so frozen shots and the baseline match the mockup. ✅ Repeatable by construction and no per-frame allocation. ❌ A duty or rate change takes effect as particles are reborn, lagging up to one 6 s life.
B) Simulate with pre-roll
A per-frame particle and packet simulation, pre-rolled one 6 s lifetime at start and before each frozen render with a fixed step. Effort M (human ~4h / CC ~20 min), risk medium, maintenance medium. ✅ Ramps react at once, and richer motion such as gusts is possible later. ✅ Familiar particle-system model. ❌ Pre-roll steps at start and on every frozen render, and repeatability depends on the fixed step.
C) Leave unspecified
Implementer picks a model; frozen shots may show empty towers. Effort S, zero now, risk high. ✅ No design work in this review. ✅ Leaves room for any library later. ❌ The C28 hero baseline and README shots would show no vapour and clumped packets.

State: approved
Actual answer: A "Closed form in time (recommended)", D2, 2026-10-14
Accepted scope: vapour particles and packets are closed-form functions of scene time and seed (vapour particle i: age (t + offset_i) mod 6 s, shown when i < 60 x duty; packet j: phase (2.5 t + 1.2 j) mod line length, below the rate cap); a duty or rate change takes effect as indices are reborn (lag up to one 6 s life); applied to chunks 09 and 10; E27 and E28 stay pending
History: none

| Sign panels and pad numbers | one mesh per hall (C24) | one InstancedMesh for all panels and one for all pad numbers, atlas region per instance | one mesh and one material per panel or number | one mesh per hall, switched instantly |

| D7 200 ms fade (approved) | required | kept | kept | broken |
| Vapour life fade | unspecified | in over 0.5 s, out over the last 1.5 s of each 6 s life [estimated] | in the custom shader | size only; particles pop at rebirth |

Question D3:
D3 — E27: How do sign panels, slot numbers and vapour particles fade one at a time while sharing materials? Project: Synapse Horizon, branch phase-3-world-building, eng review of Phase 3. ELI10: Approved rules say signs fade over 200 ms when they become too small or turn away (D7), every mesh uses shared library materials (04c), and vapour particles restart in place (D2), so they need to fade in and out or they pop. A shared material has one opacity for everything that uses it, and three's built-in materials can't fade a single instance. Three callers need the same small trick. Stakes if we pick wrong: signs and particles pop, or the shared-material rule breaks and the dispose guard stops covering sign materials. Recommendation: A because one tested helper serves all three callers, keeps the shared-material rule, and even merges every sign panel into a single draw, which fits the engineering preference for shared code with real callers. Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10, C=4/10. Net: A adds one shader patch; B adds many materials and a custom shader; C drops the fades.
Header: Fade method
Options:
A) Shared instance-opacity patch (recommended)
One helper in materials.ts adds per-instance opacity (and an atlas UV rect for text) to library materials via onBeforeCompile; panels and pad numbers become one InstancedMesh each; vapour fades in 0.5 s, out 1.5 s. Effort M (human ~4h / CC ~20 min), risk medium (tied to three's shader chunk names), maintenance low. ✅ Keeps the 04c shared-material rule and D7's 200 ms fade for every caller. ✅ All sign panels draw in one call, under C24's per-hall budget. ❌ The patch depends on three's shader chunk names, so a three upgrade must rerun the e2e fade checks.
B) Clones plus vapour shader
A material clone per sign panel and pad number; a custom ShaderMaterial for vapour. Effort M (human ~4h / CC ~20 min), risk low, maintenance medium. ✅ Plain material.opacity fades with no shader patching for signs. ✅ Full control of the vapour look in its own shader. ❌ Breaks the 04c shared-material rule for signs, and the dispose guard must track every clone.
C) No fades
Signs and numbers switch instantly; vapour fades by size only. Effort S, zero extra, risk medium. ✅ Nothing to build beyond visibility toggles. ✅ No shader code anywhere. ❌ Breaks D7's 200 ms fade, and vapour particles visibly pop as they restart.

State: approved
Actual answer: A "Shared instance-opacity patch (recommended)", D3, 2026-10-14
Accepted scope: one helper in `src/scene/materials.ts` adds a per-instance `instanceOpacity` attribute and, for atlas text, a per-instance UV rectangle to library materials through `onBeforeCompile` with a fixed `customProgramCacheKey`; sign panels (all halls) and slot-pad numbers each become one InstancedMesh using it; vapour fades in over 0.5 s and out over the last 1.5 s of each 6 s life [estimated]; tests: a unit test feeds the helper a stand-in shader and asserts the injected attribute and opacity multiply, and e2e checks a panel's opacity goes from 1 to 0 within about 200 ms after zooming out; applied to the Phase 3 heading and chunks 06, 08 and 09; E28 stays pending

Question D4:
D4 — E28: Should Phase 3 set triangle budgets now? Project: Synapse Horizon, branch phase-3-world-building, eng review of Phase 3. ELI10: Every mesh is made of triangles, and the GPU pays for each one. The plan says "low poly" but gives no numbers; chunk 36 will add a CI test with triangle budgets later, also without numbers. The campus is built now, so now is when a 2,000-triangle tree copied 150 times would slip in. Estimated, the full 12-hall campus needs about 110k triangles. Stakes if we pick wrong: a heavy part lands unnoticed and chunk 36 finds it on the M1 Air, or we add tests that pin numbers too early. Recommendation: A because per-part caps catch the one heavy part at the chunk that adds it, cost one count per builder test, and hand chunk 36 its numbers. Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10, C=4/10. Net: A guards each part now; B guards only the total; C waits for chunk 36.

A) Per-part caps and a total (recommended)
Unit tests count each builder's triangles against caps (hall body 2,000, tower 600, tree 60, car 120 and so on), plus an e2e total of 150k or less at 12 placed halls [estimated]. Effort S (human ~2h / CC ~10 min), risk low, maintenance low. ✅ A heavy part fails the test in the chunk PR that adds it. ✅ Chunk 36 starts from written, measured numbers. ❌ Caps are estimates now and may need one raise when a part's look is tuned.

One e2e reads HUD triangles at 12 placed halls, 150k or less [estimated]. Effort S (human ~1h / CC ~5 min), risk medium, maintenance low. ✅ One number to maintain, no per-part tuning. ✅ Still catches a large regression across the whole campus. ❌ A heavy part hides inside the total until it is large, and the failure does not say which part.
C) Leave to chunk 36
No triangle checks in Phase 3; chunk 36 sets budgets later. Effort S, zero now, risk medium. ✅ No numbers to guess before the look is final. ✅ Nothing to update while parts are tuned. ❌ Heavy parts can land in chunks 06-10 and surface only on the M1 Air in chunk 36.

Question D5:
D5 — E29: Should "render shadows only when something moves" go on the TODO list? Project: Synapse Horizon, branch phase-3-world-building, eng review of Phase 3. ELI10: The sun-shadow picture is redrawn every frame, even in the calm 30 fps mode, although almost nothing that casts a shadow moves on the campus. Drawing it only when a hall, fan or vehicle moves would save GPU work on a tab left open all day. It needs care: anything that moves must say so, or its shadow freezes in place. ```text
  Source status (C34)                 invalid: anything after closed except a fresh start()
  idle ──start()──► connecting ──► catching_up ──► live ──stop()──► closed
                        │               │            │
                        └──────────────►└──► error ◄─┘   (error ──stop()──► closed)
  The mock skips connecting (nothing to connect to). stop() from any state ends in closed, is idempotent,
  and drops any batch or status produced after it (a generation counter checked before delivery).
```

### Section 4: Data flow and interaction edge cases (chunk 11)

```text
  source batch ─► safeParse per event ─► dedupe by id ─► reduce (pure) ─► one set() ─► selectors ─► panel
     │ empty: no set() (C38)  │ invalid: drop+count (C36)  │ dup: skip+count (C38)  │ throw: no commit, status error (C36)
     │ out of order: lastSeen/status by max ts; sums order-free (C38)
     └ after stop(): dropped by generation check (C34)
```

Async ordering. Invariant: after any batches, totals equal the totals of the distinct valid events, and each session's `lastSeen` and `status` equal those of its greatest-`ts` event. Schedules: (1) `e2(ts 10)` then `e1(ts 5)`: with C38 `lastSeen` stays 10; (2) `e1` twice (reconnect overlap): the second is skipped by id. Single-threaded `applyBatch` with one `set()` means no interleaving inside a batch; across batches, C38's rules are order-free. Regression proof: the duplicate and shuffle tests (C38) and the after-stop test (C34).

| Interaction | Edge case | Handled | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dev source switch (off / mock) | double click | Y | `stop()` idempotent, `start()` on a running source is a no-op (C34) |
| Dev source switch | switch off mid-tick | Y | generation check (C34) |
| Session row click (C32) | session's events evicted | Y | empty state (C32) |
| Session list | zero sessions | needs rule | Section 11 |
| Session list | large list (chunk 14 backfill, thousands) | needs rule | Section 11 |
| Reload under `freeze=1` | same image | Y | catch-up batch only (C33) |

### Section 5: Code quality (chunk 11)

- Fits existing patterns: one slice file (`src/app/store/data.ts`) beside `ui.ts` and `toasts.ts`; `resetStore` resets it.
- Guidance (no new behaviour): keep the reducers as pure functions in `src/data/reduce.ts`, so they run in Node tests and in `mock:dump` without the store; the slice only calls them and commits.
- Duplicated behaviour: none; the RNG is reused (`src/sim/rng.ts`, CEO W-RW37).
- Complexity: `reduce` will branch on 9 event types; split one handler per type to keep each under 5 branches.
- Over-engineering check: the status channel (C34) is used by 3 later sources; the seen-set (C38) is bounded. No abstractions without a caller.

No issues beyond those decided above.

### Section 7: Performance (chunk 11)

- Memory: ring buffer 50,000 events at about 0.5 KB each, about 25 MB [estimated]; the C38 seen-id set about 2 MB [estimated]; aggregates scale with sessions (hundreds), negligible.
- Per batch: `safeParse` per event (C36) plus reduce; cost at 500 events per batch is unmeasured [estimated well under one frame]; chunk 14's backfill is where it matters, and its acceptance already measures load.
- Bundle: zod enters through `zod/mini` with a measured +15 KB gzip budget (C40).
- Renders: throttled to 250 ms and counted (C39).
- Slow paths: (1) a 500-event batch with many new sessions (map copies), (2) the C32 peek scanning the ring buffer (50,000 scan per click, about 1 ms [estimated]; acceptable for a dev click), (3) `mock:dump --minutes` large (Node only).

### Section 8: Observability (chunk 11)

- In place from decisions: `dataHealth.invalid` and `dataHealth.duplicates` counters (C36, C38), `source.status` (C34), `[data]` warning and error lines with context (C36).
- Gap: no record of source status changes, applied totals or batch timing outside the panel, so a report like "totals froze after an hour" cannot be traced from the console. Pending C41.

Resolved by C41: status transition lines and a health row in the panel. Alerts and dashboards: none for a dev-only chunk; the user-facing server-down banner and catch-up bar are chunks 14 and 32 (design D10, D11), and they read the C34 status. Runbook: "totals look wrong" means check the health row (invalid, duplicates), then the `[data]` lines.

#### Accepted obligations (CEO, chunk 12)

- Accepted obligations from the CEO review (2026-10-15). This list is new work for chunk 12, not existing repo state.
- Scenario registry `SCENARIOS` (one Node-runnable module in `src/data/`) lists exactly `steady`, `burst`, `churn`, `overflow`, `errors`, `codex-only`, `waiting`, each with a one-line description and its base plan (expected-shape numbers live in the tests); the params allowlist, `mock:dump`, the dev Data section and tests read scenario names from it. `mockEvents(seed, scenario, fromMs, toMs)` accepts each name, throws naming the valid names for any other, stays pure (no `Date.now()`, timers or env), and for every scenario the output over [0, 20 min) equals the concatenation over [0, 7 min) and [7 min, 20 min).
- Each scenario is a lane plan in the existing slot model; the registry names each scenario's base plan. `steady` stays byte-identical to chunk 11: `plan(seed)` keeps its `createRng` draw order and chunk 11's steady fixture test stays as the guard. Scenario variants are transforms applied after `plan(seed)` has built the steady lanes (all steady draws still taken); extra lanes draw from a separate rng seeded from `seed` and the scenario name. Base plans: `burst` = steady main lanes with the steady subagent lanes dropped after planning, lane 0's vendor forced to `claude`, plus 10 subagent lanes whose parent is lane 0, starting together every 120 sim s from 90 s and living 60 s (so the cycle [570, 630) s covers the frozen frame at 600 s), each cycle with new session ids; `churn` = 6 project lanes from the fixed `/work/` list, each periodic like the existing `SUB_PERIOD`/`SUB_LIFE` lanes (period 120 sim s, active 60 sim s, phase offset 20 sim s x project index, a new `sessionId` per cycle, no turns: `session_start`, tool call/result and usage events, then `session_end`), so at every 20 sim-s boundary one project appears and one vanishes; `overflow` = one project that starts one new main lane every 15 sim s from 480 s until 40 exist (8 during the catch-up, the rest growing live), plus one second project with 2 main lanes; `errors` = the steady plan, where a storm repeats every 300 sim s: in [270 + 300n, 330 + 300n) s, so [570, 630) s covers the frozen frame at 600 s, at least 5 main lanes emit an `error` event (status `error`) at offset 990 ms of each slot with their normal events suppressed, then one `thinking` status event at the window end (after the storm at connect ends at 630 s, the next starts at 870 s, 27 real s after connect at 10x); `codex-only` = the steady plan with every lane vendor `codex`; `waiting` = the steady plan where at least 3 main lanes end a turn with `waiting_user` by 590 sim s and emit no status-bearing event after it.
- Acceptance window: "within 60 s at 10x" means 60 real s at 10x after the 10 sim-minute catch-up, so tests cover sim [0, 1,200,000 ms). Shape tests reduce the scenario in 1 sim-s steps through `applyBatch` and sample after each step; a sample "at T" is the state after applying every event with sim ms < T + 1,000 (the whole slot that starts at T). Every scenario also asserts its signature shape at exactly 600 s, the frozen frame. Expected shapes (plan-chosen [estimated] numbers, tunable by eng review): `steady` keeps chunk 11's fixture totals at 600 s; `burst` has exactly 10 subagents with status not `done` sharing one parent `sessionId` at 120 s, 240 s and 600 s, and 0 at 60 s and 180 s; `churn` has exactly 3 active projects at every sample from 100 s on, and each 20 sim-s boundary from 120 s on swaps exactly one project in and one out, with every key under `/work/`; `overflow` has one project with exactly 9 main sessions at 600 s, 29 at 900 s and 40, none `done`, at 1,200 s, so it passes the 16- and 32-session hall thresholds live and stays under the D8 cap of 48; `errors` has at least 5 sessions with status `error` at 300 s, 600 s and 900 s, and 0 at 400 s, 700 s and 1,000 s; `codex-only` has every event vendor `codex`, at least 3 projects and 5 main sessions; `waiting` has at least 3 sessions whose latest status is `waiting_user` at 600 s and at 1,200 s, and the event stream shows no `turn_start` for those sessions in [590 s, 1,200 s).
- Pure selector `activeProjects(state)`: projects with at least one main session whose status is not `done` (needed because reducers never remove projects; used by the churn assertion and later by the chunk 19 reconciler); unit-tested.
- Clock contract `SimClock` in `src/data/clock.ts` (Node-runnable): `createSimClock({ realNow, startMs, speed, paused })` returns an object with `now()`, read-only getters `speed` and `paused`, and `play()`, `pause()`, `setSpeed(s)`. `now()` returns source time in epoch ms (the time base of event `ts`), so every source and chunk 13's inference share one time base: the mock starts at `ANCHOR_MS + CATCHUP_MS` and converts with sim ms = `now() - ANCHOR_MS`; a live source starts at the injected local wall clock and runs at 1x (logs are local files written on the same machine, so the only gap is delivery delay; chunk 13 treats an event `ts` later than `now()` as `now()`); file replay (chunk 17) sets its own `startMs`. `speed` is 1, 10 or 60; `setSpeed` with any other value changes nothing and logs one `[data]` warning. Pausing or changing speed rebases so source time never jumps or goes back; while paused `now()` is constant. Unit tests with a fake `realNow` cover each transition and the invalid speed.
- Clock ownership: `App.tsx` (and the dev Data section) creates one clock per connection with `startMs` = `ANCHOR_MS + CATCHUP_MS`, passes it to `createMockSource({ seed, scenario, freeze, clock })`, and calls `connect(source, clock)`. `MockSource` reads sim time only from that clock; `createMockSource` no longer calls `performance.now()`. The store keeps the clock reference and mirrors `speed` and `paused` in state; store actions `play`, `pause`, `setSpeed` call the clock and update the mirror. `connect(source)` without a clock (a live source) creates a 1x running clock whose controls are disabled, so chunk 13 inference still reads one store clock for every source. Every mock `connect` starts at the end of the catch-up (sim 10 min). Ticks stay every 250 ms real time; at 60x one tick spans 15 sim s, still delivered in batches of at most `MAX_BATCH`.
- Speed equivalence: after sim time T = 1,200 s (a multiple of the 15 sim-s tick at 60x), `projects`, `sessions`, `subagents`, `tokens` and the ring contents are identical whether reached at 1x, 10x or 60x (fake clock test); `dataHealth` batch counts and timings are excluded.
- Pause: while paused, N ticks deliver zero events and make zero store commits (state reference unchanged); after `play()` the delivered events equal an unpaused run over the same sim range, with no gap and no duplicate.
- G12 store half: connect a `FakeSource` named `live`, then the mock, then the live fake again; final totals equal the live fake alone, with 0 duplicates.
- G18 store half: `play`, `pause` and `setSpeed` change the sim range delivered per tick as expected (10x delivers 10x the sim range of 1x per tick); the UI half (top-bar chip and replay bar) is tested in chunk 27.
- URL params through the `parseParams` allowlist: `scenario` accepts the 7 registry names, `speed` accepts `1`, `10`, `60`; any other value warns and falls back (`steady`, `1`); `speed` or `scenario` without `source=mock` warns that it is ignored; tests cover each accepted value and one rejected value of each.
- Under `freeze=1` the clock starts paused at the catch-up end with speed forced to 1 whatever the URL says, and each `play`/`setSpeed` call is a no-op that logs one `[data]` info line, so frozen captures hold exactly the catch-up events for any scenario and speed.
- `vp run mock:dump` accepts all 7 scenarios; an unknown scenario exits non-zero naming the valid ones.
- Dev Data section (dev=1 only; interim until chunk 27 builds the D8 chip and replay bar; TASTE decision 6): scenario select, play/pause and 1x/10x/60x buttons acting through the store actions, disabled for a live source and under `freeze=1`. Choosing a scenario reconnects with a new clock at the catch-up end, keeps the current speed, starts running (paused under `freeze=1`) and leaves the URL unchanged. These controls take precedence over the chunk text "the dev menu only adds seed and debug toggles" until chunk 27, unless the user overrides TASTE decision 6 at the final gate. The health row adds, for mock and replay sources, source time as +HH:MM:SS since `ANCHOR_MS` for the mock (+00:10:00 at the end of the catch-up; the replay base is defined in chunk 17; no time zone, so frozen captures match on every machine), plus speed and paused (X2).
- README "Data sources" gains a scenarios table (name, what it shows, URL such as `?source=mock&scenario=burst&speed=10`); a unit test fails if a registry scenario is missing from the README table.
- `MockSource.tick` catches a throw from the generator or the batch callback, reports `onStatus("error", detail)` once naming the scenario and sim range, and stops ticking; unit test with an injected `generate` that throws.
- Per-tick cap: one tick delivers at most 60 sim s (four 60x ticks). When the clock is further ahead (a hidden tab whose timers were throttled, or a stalled main thread), the source reports `catching_up`, delivers the next 60 sim s on each tick until it reaches `now()`, then reports `live`. Unit test: advance the fake real clock by 10 real minutes at 60x in one step; no tick delivers more than 60 sim s, status goes `catching_up` then `live`, and the final aggregates equal an uncapped run.
- Clock transitions log one `[data]` line each (`[data] clock: 1x -> 10x`, `[data] clock: paused`, `[data] clock: playing`); unit test counts the lines.
- One Playwright check under `dev=1&source=mock&scenario=burst&speed=10`: Pause stops the applied count changing over 1 s, Play resumes it.
- Re-capture `11-store-debug.png` in this PR, since the health row gains the clock fields (frozen: +00:10:00, 1x, paused).
- Code layout: lane plans and scenario transforms live in the registry module; `mockEvents` and `laneEvents` stay generic and read per-lane fields (end slot, period, no-turns, error windows) instead of branching on scenario names.
- Build order inside the chunk: clock, store actions, params and the G12/G18 store halves first, then the registry, scenarios and README, so a scenario-tuning failure cannot hold up the clock that chunks 13, 17 and 27 need.
- TODOS.md gains four entries: P2 bound the growth of `done` sessions in the store (churn and burst add a new session id per cycle, up to 18,000 per real hour at 60x [estimated: burst adds 10 subagent ids per 120 sim s, churn 6], and `applyBatch` copies the whole sessions map per batch; trigger: chunk 13 session-end inference); when chunk 27 lands, remove the interim dev-HUD clock controls or keep them as debug-only so two control surfaces never drive the clock; and the two CEO deferrals: P3 seekable replay clock (X1; seek = reconnect at a new `startMs` with the store cleared, so no consumer ever sees time go back; trigger: chunk 27 replay bar or chunk 17 wants scrubbing) and P3 `tour` demo scenario (X4, trigger: a demo or README video needs one URL that shows everything).

#### Section 1: Architecture (chunk 12)
```
 URL ─► parseParams (scenario, speed, seed, freeze) ─► App.tsx
                                                         │ creates per connection
                                                         ▼
              SCENARIOS registry ◄──────────── SimClock(realNow, startMs, speed, paused)
   (names, base plans, transforms)                ▲ play/pause/setSpeed     │ now() epoch ms
     │        │         │       │                 │                         ▼
     ▼        ▼         ▼       ▼          store clock actions     MockSource.tick (250 ms real)
 mock.ts  params.ts  mock-dump DataSection ──────┘                  mockEvents(seed, scenario,
 (generic lanes)                (dev=1)                              last, min(now, last+60 s))
                                                                            │ ≤ 500 per batch
                                                                            ▼
                         store.connect(source, clock) ─► ingest ─► applyBatch ─► aggregates, ring
                                                                     selectors: activeProjects, sessionList
```
Clock state machine:
```
            play()                     setSpeed(1|10|60): rebase, keep state
  PAUSED ─────────────► RUNNING(speed) ◄──┐
     ▲                      │             │ setSpeed (rebase)
     └──────── pause() ─────┘─────────────┘
  FROZEN (freeze=1): PAUSED, speed 1; play/setSpeed = no-op + one [data] line
  Invalid: speed outside {1,10,60} -> no change + warning; now() going back -> impossible (rebase anchors
  sim time at the transition instant)
```
Findings: the dev scenario switch creates a new clock and source and goes through `connect`, so the existing token guard (src/app/store/data.ts:46-56) drops callbacks of the old pair; no new coupling beyond `params.ts` importing the registry from `src/data` (Node-runnable, allowed direction). Scaling at 60x with `overflow` [estimated: 40 lanes x 15 slots x about 1.5 events = about 900 events per tick, 2 batches, about 3,600 events/s]: `applyBatch` copies three Maps per batch of at most ~50 sessions, fine; the 50,000-event ring turns over in about 14 s, eviction is O(1). Single point of failure: the clock; covered by transition tests. Rollback: revert the PR, minutes; no data or schema change. No artifact-about-the-work added.

#### Section 4: Data Flow & Interaction Edge Cases (chunk 12)
```
 URL/dev control ─► VALIDATE (allowlist) ─► SimClock ─► tick range ─► mockEvents ─► validate ─► applyBatch ─► set()
   shadow: bad value -> fallback   paused -> empty range, no set()   range > 60 s -> capped, catching_up
           speed w/o mock -> warn  invalid speed -> unchanged         throw -> status error, stop
           empty range -> no batch duplicate id -> skipped (existing)
```
| Interaction | Edge case | Handled? | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Play/Pause | double click | Y | idempotent clock methods |
| setSpeed while paused | stays paused, speed updates | Y | rebase on resume |
| Scenario switch while paused | new clock running (paused under freeze) | Y | accepted bullet |
| StrictMode double mount | two clocks | Y | disconnect stops the first source |
| Tab hidden at 60x | one huge tick | Y (new) | per-tick cap |
| Switch to live while mock paused | live clock 1x running | Y | live clock created on connect |
Async ordering: one shared state (the store) and one writer per connection; the token guard excludes the old source's late ticks after `connect`; both orders (old tick before or after connect) end with only the new source's batches applied, as chunk 11's E30 test shows.

- Frozen frame (replaces "Every scenario also asserts its signature shape at exactly 600 s"): the frozen-frame assertion is the state after applying `mockEvents(seed, scenario, 0, CATCHUP_MS)`, exactly what `freeze=1` holds. Expected frozen shapes: `burst` 10 live subagents under one parent; `churn` 3 active projects; `overflow` 8 main sessions in the growing project (replaces "exactly 9 main sessions at 600 s"); `errors` at least 5 sessions with status `error`; `waiting` at least 3 sessions with latest status `waiting_user`; `steady` and `codex-only` their 600 s totals. Slot-inclusive samples "at T" keep their meaning for every other T.
- Base plans list exactly which steady lanes survive: `churn` and `overflow` drop all steady lanes; `codex-only` keeps the steady main lanes with vendor `codex` and drops the steady subagent lanes (they are hard-coded `claude`); `burst`, `errors` and `waiting` keep the steady main lanes as stated.
- Steady guard: before the lane refactor, commit SHA-256 digests of the JSON-serialised `steady` stream for seeds 1 and 42 over [0, 1,200 s); a test asserts them after the refactor.
- Pause and backlog (replaces the CEO pause bullet): pause freezes `now()`; ticks keep draining [last, now()) under the per-tick cap; once caught up, N paused ticks deliver zero events and make zero store commits, and `play()` resumes with no gap and no duplicate. The pause test first reaches the caught-up state.
- Hidden tab (replaces the CEO hidden-tab rationale; TASTE 16 revised): a mock or replay clock auto-pauses while `document.visibilityState` is `hidden` and resumes on `visible` (rebase, no jump); a user pause stays paused when the tab becomes visible again. The per-tick cap of 60 sim s stays as the guard for main-thread stalls, with hysteresis: the source reports `catching_up` only when more than one cap behind and `live` only when fully caught up. Tests: hidden then visible delivers a continuous stream; steady 1 Hz ticks at 60x cause no status changes.
- Catch-up throw: `MockSource.start` applies the same catch as `tick` around the initial catch-up, reporting `onStatus("error", detail)` once with scenario and range and not scheduling ticks; the injected-`generate` test covers both paths.
- Live clock: the live (1x, no controls) clock reads `now() = max(previous, wallNow())` from the injected wall clock, so laptop sleep or clock adjustment cannot leave it behind event time; mock and replay clocks keep rebasing on the monotonic `realNow`.
- Locked clocks: the clock has a `locked` flag (live, and every clock under `freeze=1`); a locked `play`, `pause` or `setSpeed` changes nothing and logs one `[data]` line per call. The store mirror of `speed` and `paused` is always read back from the clock getters after an action, never set from the requested value.
- One clock owner (replaces "`connect(source, clock)`"): a source exposes `readonly clock?: SimClock`; `createMockSource` creates the clock inside the same `App.tsx` effect that calls `connect(source)`; `connect` reads `source.clock` and creates a locked 1x live clock when it is absent. Each reconnect, including a StrictMode remount and a dev scenario switch, gets a fresh clock.
- Clock edge cases pinned in tests: `setSpeed` while paused changes the speed and stays paused; `setSpeed(current)` changes nothing and logs nothing.
- Module layout (TASTE 25, smaller arrangement): `src/data/scenarios.ts` is a leaf module with the scenario names and descriptions only (imported by `params.ts`, `mock-dump.ts`, the dev section, tests and the README check); lane plans and transforms live in `src/data/mock.ts`. New files: `src/data/clock.ts`, `src/data/scenarios.ts`. This replaces "lane plans and scenario transforms live in the registry module".
- Playwright pause check precondition: wait for status `live` and an increasing applied count before pressing Pause.
- UC1 detail (approved at the final gate): `sourceEpoch` increments on every `connect` (including a scenario switch on the same source type) and on `disconnect`; both are unit-tested.
- TODOS.md also gains: chunk 13 must re-run the `waiting` and `churn` shape tests after session-end inference lands, since 30-minute idle-end marks waiting sessions `done` at about 2,390 sim s (waiting lanes may need a non-status heartbeat).

### Taste decisions (CEO)

- T1 token refresh after restart: chosen same-origin `GET /api/session` refresh (P5 explicit, keeps eng A1 per-run token). Alternative: reload the page on 4401; simpler, but loses the open tab's state and breaks the G4 "open tab recovers" acceptance.
- T2 watcher backend: chosen Node recursive `fs.watch` plus 5 s rescan (P3 pragmatic, reuse ladder rung 2: stdlib before a dependency; one handle per root avoids macOS EMFILE with thousands of JSONL files). Alternative: keep chokidar v4 (the 02b choice), which starts `fs.watch` watchers for every path under the roots. Reverses a 02b dependency choice, so surfaced.

### User challenges (CEO)

- UC1 Dependabot prefix for runtime dependencies. You said (PR #8, b17f26e): npm updates use `build(deps)`, which cuts no release. CEO C8 (approved 2026-10-12) said runtime deps use `fix(deps)` so `ws` and watcher fixes reach the binaries. Recommendation: `prefix: "fix(deps)"` for runtime deps, keep `prefix-development: "chore(deps)"`. Why: from chunk 14 on, runtime deps ship inside the 14b binaries; under `build(deps)` a security fix waits for the next unrelated `feat`/`fix`. Blind spot: you may have switched to avoid a patch release on every weekly frontend bump (react, three); that cost is real (about one patch release a week). Cost if wrong: weekly patch releases with 4 binaries each (noise), or, the other way, a known-vulnerable `ws` in shipped binaries for weeks.

- UC2 Binary release timing. You said (CEO C1, chunk 14b "Depends on: 02b, 14"): 4-OS binaries start once the binary tails real logs. Both reviews here (primary and independent CEO voice, both Claude; Codex disabled) recommend making 14b depend on chunk 15 too, so the first public binary shows real Claude Code sessions instead of per-file line counts. Why: after 14 the binary can only show a line counter and the mock demo; a first download is the product's first impression. Blind spot: you may want the release pipeline proven early, independent of parser risk; chunk 14's local `build:bin` check proves the bundle on the Mac only. Cost if wrong: either a weak first download (keep as is) or the 4-OS pipeline proven one chunk later (change).

- Chunk 13: `Metric` is `{ value: number | null, unit, provenance, basis }`; `null` means unknown and every formatter renders it as "unknown" (G7: an unknown model's cost is `null`, never 0). Unit test: unknown model gives `value: null` and formatted "unknown".
- Chunk 13: session-end inference runs through one store action `advanceTo(nowMs)`, called after every applied batch and on every source tick (also when a tick delivers no events); a session whose last activity is at T ends at exactly T + 30 min (its end `ts` is that value, never the tick time), so G6 holds at 1x, 10x and 60x; `advanceTo` is a no-op while the clock is paused or when `nowMs` is not later than the last call. Test: the same session ends at the same sim ms at 1x and 60x, and N paused ticks make no store commit.
- Chunk 13: tokens/min is the trailing 60 sim s window, kept in per-session one-second buckets (not read from the ring buffer); the inlet first-order lag (tau 30 s) is integrated exactly in sim time between input changes, so derived values at a sim time T are identical at 1x, 10x and 60x. Test: speed-equivalence of every derived selector at T = 1,200 s.
- Chunk 13 (X1): sessions and subagents with status `done` are evicted from the `sessions`/`subagents` maps once they are no longer in the ring buffer, with project and global token totals unchanged. Test: a 2-hour `churn` run at 60x keeps the map size bounded (at most active sessions plus the ring-buffer-referenced ones) and totals equal to an uncompacted run.
- Chunk 13 (X4): the price table carries `asOf` (YYYY-MM) and every cost `basis` names it (for example "tokens x claude-opus price, prices as of 2026-10"). Test: basis string contains `asOf`.
- Chunk 14 (C70): the log-server middleware registers in both `configureServer` and `configurePreviewServer`, so `vp preview` and every Playwright run serve the WebSocket; e2e sets `SYNAPSE_LOG_ROOTS` to a per-test temp fixture dir and never reads the real home directory. Test: the "appended line shows within 1 s" check runs in Playwright against preview.
- Chunk 14 (C72): a dropped WebSocket is retried inside the live source with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped at 10 s) without calling the store's `connect` and without bumping `sourceEpoch`; on reopen the client sends its per-file byte cursors and the server resumes from them; `SourceStatus` gains `reconnecting`, which the pill shows. Test: kill and restart the server under a fake source socket; totals equal an uninterrupted run with 0 duplicates (G4).
- Chunk 14 (C73): under `vp dev` the plugin's Host and Origin checks accept the Vite server's own resolved origin (`localhost:<port>` per #9); under `vp preview` and the binary they accept `127.0.0.1:<port>`; any other Host gets 421 and any other Origin is refused. Chunk 01 text and the C2 note are corrected to describe #9. Tests: upgrade with `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<other>` refused; `Host: evil.example:<port>` refused under dev, preview and binary.
- Chunk 14 (C79): `source=live` is the default when no `source` param is given; `source=mock` selects the mock; `parseParams` accepts `live` and `mock`. When the log server is unreachable the D11 banner shows and the D9 card's "Try the demo" switches to `source=mock&scenario=steady`. Test: params and a Playwright check that a page without `source` opens the WebSocket.
- Chunk 14 (X2): log roots resolve, in order, from `SYNAPSE_LOG_ROOTS` (path-delimiter separated), the binary's repeatable `--logs <dir>`, the `roots` array of the config file (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/synapse-horizon/config.json`, else `~/.config/synapse-horizon/config.json`, on Windows `%APPDATA%\synapse-horizon\config.json`; a missing file is normal, an unreadable or invalid one logs one `[logs]` line and falls through), then defaults `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` (else `~/.claude/projects`) and `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (else `~/.codex/sessions`), all through `os.homedir()` and `path`. Tests per OS path style with mocked env and homedir.
- Chunk 14 (X3): at start the server logs one `[logs]` line per root: resolved path and file count modified within 24 h, or the reason it is missing or unreadable (G5). Test asserts the lines.
- Chunk 14b (C78): a `report` job with `needs: [release, build]` and `if: always() && needs.build.result != 'success' && needs.release.outputs.published == 'true'` writes the "Incomplete: builds missing for <os list>" prefix; the checksums job removes it once all 4 binaries exist. Test: `scripts/release-workflow.test.ts` asserts the job graph and conditions.
- Chunk 14b (X5): each matrix smoke starts the binary with `--no-open --port 4400 --logs <fixture dir>`, appends one line to a fixture file, and reads a line-count message over the WebSocket using the injected token, besides the existing HTTP, `--version` and heartbeat checks; Windows steps use `shell: bash`.
- Chunk 14 (taste T1): when the server rejects the token (close code 4401, or 401 on HTTP), the live source fetches a fresh token once from `GET /api/session` (same Host and Origin gates, requires `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when the header is present, no CORS headers, `Cache-Control: no-store`) and reconnects; a second rejection sets status `error` with the reason. Tests: restart with a new token recovers without reload; a cross-origin fetch of `/api/session` gets no readable body; `Host: evil.example` gets 421.
- Chunk 14 (taste T2): the watcher uses Node's built-in `fs.watch(root, { recursive: true })` per root (one handle per root on macOS and Windows) plus a 5 s stat rescan of known files as a backstop for missed events, instead of chokidar; no `chokidar` dependency is added. Tests: append, create, truncate and rotate fixtures are seen within 1 s through events and within 6 s with events disabled (rescan only).
- Chunk 13 (spec 1.1): a cost total over sessions where some models are unknown sums only the known ones and its `basis` says "excludes N sessions with unknown model"; it is `null` ("unknown") only when every session is unknown. Tests: mixed, all-known, all-unknown.
- Chunk 13 (spec 1.2): evicted session ids go into a tombstone set capped at 100,000 ids (oldest dropped); a later event for a tombstoned id reactivates it as an active session without incrementing the project's session count again, and project and global totals still add its tokens. Test: a session idle-ends, is evicted, then gets a new event 40 sim min later; counts and totals match an uncompacted run.
- Chunk 13 (spec 1.3, 1.4): every source calls `advanceTo` at least once per real second (the mock and replay on their 250 ms ticks; the live source on a 1 s timer even with no events); the store resets the last-advance mark on every `connect` and `sourceEpoch` change. Tests: a quiet live fake source idle-ends a session at T + 30 min; after a scenario switch, inference runs again.
- Chunk 13 (spec 3.5): the optional `AgentEvent` fields for jobs are `todo?: { id: string, status: "pending" | "in_progress" | "completed" }` (TodoWrite item; text goes through `currentTask`, redacted) and `toolClass?: "edit" | "git_commit" | "test" | "lint" | "other"` (classified in Node by the parsers; raw commands never reach the browser, D16). `src/config/estimation.ts` names every constant with its value and an `[estimated]` comment: `IDLE_KW = 0.8`, `KW_PER_TOKEN_PER_MIN = 0.004`, `RACK_MAX_KW = 40`, `INLET_BASE_C = 22`, `INLET_C_PER_KW = 0.25`, `HOT_AISLE_DELTA_C = 12`, `LAG_TAU_S = 30`, `HALL_COOLING_CAPACITY_KW = 400`, `IDLE_END_MS = 30 * 60_000`.
- Chunk 13 (spec 3.6): "debug panel" in the acceptance means the `dev=1` HUD Data section; it lists each metric with value, unit, badge and basis.
- Chunk 14 (spec 1.5): the 5 s rescan also re-probes missing roots and starts watching a root that appears after startup, logging one `[logs]` line; on Linux an `ENOSPC` (inotify watch limit) from `fs.watch` falls back to rescan-only for that root with one `[logs]` line naming the limit. Tests: root created after start is picked up within 6 s; injected `ENOSPC` keeps tailing via rescan.
- Chunk 14 (spec 1.8): with `freeze=1` and no explicit `source`, no source connects (today's behaviour), so every frozen screenshot baseline and `vp run shots` output is unchanged; the live default applies only without `freeze=1`. Specs that test D9, D10, D11 or the pill pass `source=live` and their own fixture roots. Test: the existing baselines pass unchanged in the chunk 14 PR.
- Chunk 14 (spec 3.2): pill mapping from `SourceStatus`: `connecting` "Connecting"; `catching_up` "Catching up n/N files" (D10, from server progress); `live` "Connected"; `reconnecting` "Reconnecting"; `closed` "Off"; `error` "Off" plus the reason in the tooltip. The D11 banner shows when the first connection fails or `reconnecting` lasts 3 s or more, and hides on `live`. The D9 card shows when the server reports zero files in every root after backfill. Test: each status renders its pill text.
- Chunk 14 (spec 3.3): the token is injected as `<meta name="synapse-token" content="...">` in the served HTML (dev via `transformIndexHtml`, preview and binary by templating `index.html` at serve time); the binary prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` and the 14b smoke reads the token from the HTML and the port from that line.
- Chunk 14 (spec 3.4): `POST /api/import` exists in chunk 14 only as a gated stub: Host, Origin and token checks, then 501 "import arrives in chunk 17". Tests cover the gate rejections and the 501.
- Chunk 14 (spec 5.3, threat model): the token is defence in depth for browsers: Origin checks stop cross-origin pages and the Host gate stops DNS rebinding; any local process can read `/api/session` or the page, so the token does not defend against local processes, which already can read the log files directly. README "Data sources and privacy" states this.
- Chunk 14 (spec 3.1, pass-2 2.2): root sources do not merge, and the order is: the binary's `--logs` first, then `SYNAPSE_LOG_ROOTS`, then the config file `roots`, then the two defaults; the first non-empty source wins, so a flag always beats an exported env var. This order replaces the X2 order above. Tests: env set plus config file gives only the env roots; `--logs` plus env gives only the `--logs` roots.
- Chunk 13 (pass-2 1.1): `waiting_user` holds until the 30-minute idle end like any other status (eng Q3), so a waiting session ends at its last event + 30 min. Re-run expectations: `waiting` keeps at least 3 sessions with latest status `waiting_user` at 600 s and 1,200 s and those sessions are `done` at their last event + 30 min (about 2,390 sim s); `churn` shapes over [0, 1,800 s) are unchanged, since every idle gap there is under 30 min or ends with `session_end`.
- Chunk 13 (pass-2 1.3): hall heat = sum of rack kW of the racks in that hall; rack load = rack kW / `RACK_MAX_KW`; hot aisle = inlet + `HOT_AISLE_DELTA_C` x mean rack load of the hall; cooling duty = min(1, total hall heat / (`HALL_COOLING_CAPACITY_KW` x placed halls)); when the unclamped value exceeds 1 the duty `basis` says "over capacity". Tests: fixed inputs for each formula, including the clamp.
- Chunk 13 (pass-2 1.4, 3.3): tombstones cover subagent ids as well as session ids. Per-session token counters of an evicted session are dropped; a reactivated session restarts its per-session counters at 0 while project and global totals stay exact; an id dropped from the full tombstone set (beyond 100,000) counts as a new session if it returns. README notes both limits.
- Chunk 13 (pass-2 3.2): the inlet lag state lives in the store and `advanceTo` integrates it exactly across every input change between the previous and the new `nowMs` (one-second bucket boundaries), so no selector holds hidden state.
- Chunk 13 and 14 (pass-2 2.1): until the top bar (chunk 27) exists, the pill sits at the right end of the existing top-bar row, the D11 banner directly below that row, and the D9 card centred in the `safeArea`, all visible without `dev=1`; `ProvenanceBadge` is shown in chunk 13 only in the `dev=1` HUD Data section. KPI shimmer (D10) moves to chunk 28 and the "(est.)" panel-label check to chunk 29.
- Chunk 14 (pass-2 1.2): a cursor is `{ path, fileId, offset }`, where `fileId` is `dev:ino` from `fs.stat` (or `birthtimeMs` where `ino` is 0 on Windows); on resume, a changed `fileId` or a file shorter than `offset` re-reads that file from 0 and the browser dedupes by event id. Tests: truncated and rotated while the server was down.
- Chunk 14 (pass-2 2.3, 3.1): Host and Origin are checked before the upgrade (421 and 403 over HTTP); the token is checked after the upgrade: the client's first message is `{ type: "hello", token, cursors }`, and a missing or wrong token within 2 s closes the socket with code 4401, which the browser can see and which triggers T1. Tests: no hello in 2 s, wrong token, and correct token.
- Chunk 14 (pass-2 3.4): the automated G4 restart test is a Node integration test that stops and restarts the real WebSocket server on the same port while a `LiveSource` (Node 24's global `WebSocket` client) stays connected; under `vp dev` a full page reload by Vite's own client on restart is acceptable and is checked manually.
- Chunk 14 (pass-2 3.5): the token meta tag is templated into every response that serves `index.html` (`/`, `/index.html` and the SPA fallback), each with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Test: all three carry the current token and the header.
- Chunk 14 (pass-2 5.1): `ws` is added as a runtime dependency and bundled into the CLI by esbuild (not external); a test asserts the CLI bundle contains no `require("ws")` left unresolved. The rescan-only and `ENOSPC` tests run in `vp test` on ubuntu in CI.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 1.1): the server sends line counts as `{ type: "lines", path, fileId, total }`, the absolute line total of that file identity (never a delta), so a re-read from 0 after rotation replaces the value instead of adding to it; backfill progress is `{ type: "progress", done, total }`, root status is `{ type: "roots", roots: [{ path, files, reason? }] }`, and heartbeats are `{ type: "heartbeat" }`, sent right after an accepted hello and then every 10 s. The message schema lives in `src/data/wire.ts` (zod/mini, Node-runnable) and is shared by server and client. Line totals go to a separate `logLines` store slice keyed by `path + fileId`, never through `applyBatch`; the `dev=1` HUD Data section lists them as `real` metrics with `data-metric`, and the Playwright "within 1 s" check reads that row. Tests: rotation replaces, reconnect resends absolute totals, schema rejects unknown types.
- Chunk 13 (pass-3 1.2): in the data layer a rack is a main session (its subagents' tokens/min add to it, section 2) and a hall is a project (D5); "placed halls" for cooling duty is the number of projects with at least one main session not `done` (`activeProjects`), with a floor of 2 because halls A and B always exist (D8). No data selector reads scene placement.
- Chunk 14b (pass-3 1.3): the `report` and `checksums` jobs each get job-level `contents: write`; `release-workflow.test.ts` asserts every job's permissions.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 2.1): e2e for the log server runs in a separate Playwright project `logserver` with its own `webServer` (`vp preview` on its own port, `SYNAPSE_LOG_ROOTS` set to `e2e/.tmp/logs`, `workers: 1`); each spec rewrites that directory before it navigates (empty for the D9 card, a fixture file for counts, an appended line for the 1 s check). The D11 banner and `reconnecting` states use Playwright `page.routeWebSocket` to refuse or drop the socket, so no server has to stop mid-run. The other projects keep their current `webServer` and never read a real home directory, because their pages connect with no `source` under `freeze=1` or with explicit `source=mock`.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 2.2): the original chunk 14 text "require a per-run random token injected into the served page" is implemented by the hello-message check above (pass-2 2.3, 3.1); an upgrade is not refused for the token alone.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 3.1): a request with no `Origin` header (non-browser local clients: the Node integration test, the 14b smoke) passes the Origin check and still needs the token; a present Origin that does not match gets 403. Tests: absent Origin with token accepted, absent Origin without token closed 4401, mismatched Origin 403.
- Chunk 14b (pass-3 3.2): the smoke's WebSocket client is a committed `scripts/smoke-ws.mjs`, run with the runner's Node 24 from setup-vp on all 4 runners, which sends the hello and waits up to 5 s for a heartbeat and a `lines` message for the appended fixture line.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 3.3): in chunk 14 the D9 card shows only "Try the demo"; "Drop a .jsonl to replay" appears with chunk 17.
- Chunk 14 (pass-3 5.2): `scripts/bundle-cli.ts` marks `bufferutil` and `utf-8-validate` external (`ws` falls back to its JS paths when they are missing); the bundle test allows exactly those two unresolved requires and fails on any other.
- Chunk 13 (CEO voice F3): the price table is keyed by model and token class (`in`, `out`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, per million tokens) and cost = the sum over the four classes; the metric's label is "API-equivalent cost" and its `basis` says it is not a subscription bill. Test: fixed input with cache-read tokens dominating gives the per-class sum, not one blended rate.
- Chunk 13 (CEO voice F7): every token or cost total in live mode names its window in `basis` ("last 24 h, backfill window"), so totals never read as all-time.
- Chunk 14 (CEO voice F10): README "Data sources and privacy" lists what reaches the browser now (per-file line counts and root paths only) and what chunk 15 will add (session ids, model, token counts, tool names, `currentTask` truncated to 120 chars and redacted, D16).

### Section 1: Architecture

```
  ~/.claude/projects  ~/.codex/sessions   (roots: --logs > SYNAPSE_LOG_ROOTS > config > CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME defaults)
          │                   │
          └── sidecar/watch.ts: fs.watch(recursive) + 5 s rescan ── sidecar/tail.ts: cursor {path,fileId,offset}
                                   │ lines/progress/roots/heartbeat (src/data/wire.ts, zod)
          sidecar/logServer.ts: Host gate → Origin gate → WS upgrade → hello{token,cursors} (4401) ── GET /api/session (T1)
             ▲ registered by            ▲ registered by              ▲ used by
     sidecar/plugin.ts               sidecar/plugin.ts            sidecar/cli.ts (binary, 127.0.0.1)
     configureServer (dev,           configurePreviewServer
     localhost per #9)               (preview, Playwright)
                                   │ same-origin WebSocket
          src/data/liveSource.ts (Source; locked live clock; reconnect 1/2/4/10 s; 1 s advance tick)
                                   ▼
          store: data slice (applyBatch, advanceTo, eviction+tombstones, jobs, lag state) + logLines slice
                 │ selectors → Metric {value|null, unit, provenance, basis}
                 ▼
          HUD Data section (dev=1) + ProvenanceBadge;  pill / D11 banner / D9 card (no dev=1)
```
Dependency change: `sidecar/*` imports only Node-runnable `src/data/wire.ts` and `schema.ts` (existing rule, E31). New coupling: `logLines` slice is separate from `applyBatch`, so chunk 15 can retire it without touching reducers. State machine (live source):

```
  idle ─connect→ connecting ─hello ok→ catching_up ─progress done→ live
     live/catching_up ─socket drop→ reconnecting ─reopen+hello→ catching_up
     reconnecting ─4401→ (refresh token once, T1) ─fail→ error
     any ─disconnect→ closed      invalid: live→connecting (only via store connect, which bumps sourceEpoch)
```
Scaling: 10x files is cheap on macOS/Windows (one handle per root); on Linux the inotify watch count grows per directory (ENOSPC fallback). 100x backfill: 24 h of lines streamed as per-file totals, not lines, so payload stays small in chunk 14; chunk 15 batches events at 500. Single points of failure: the server process (banner D11, reconnect). Security architecture: Section 3. Rollback: each chunk is one squash PR; revert ships a patch (02b runbook). Findings: PR1-PR4, PR7, PR8 (all dispositioned in the ledger). Value test: no process-only artifacts added; `[logs]` lines and the pill are product observability.

| Codepath | What can go wrong | Class | Rescued | Action | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roots resolve | env/config path missing | ENOENT | Y | `[logs]` line, root marked missing | pill tooltip reason (G5) |
| roots resolve | config JSON invalid | SyntaxError / zod | Y | `[logs]` line, fall through | defaults used |
| watch | fd/inotify limit | EMFILE / ENOSPC | Y | rescan-only for root, `[logs]` line | nothing, slower updates |
| watch | root deleted at runtime | ENOENT | Y | re-probe every 5 s | pill reason |
| tail | file truncated / rotated | size < offset, fileId change | Y | re-read from 0, absolute totals | correct counts |
| tail | partial last line | no newline | Y | hold bytes until newline | nothing |
| tail | read permission | EACCES | Y | skip file, `[logs]` line, count in `roots` | pill reason |
| WS upgrade | bad Host | gate | Y | 421 + stderr line | n/a (attacker) |
| WS upgrade | bad Origin | gate | Y | 403 | n/a |
| WS hello | missing/wrong token | 4401 | Y | client refreshes once (T1) | "Reconnecting", then error reason |
| WS send | slow client backpressure | bufferedAmount high | Y | drop to latest absolute totals per file | nothing |
| live source | server down | close 1006 / connect fail | Y | backoff 1/2/4/10 s | D11 banner after 3 s |
| wire parse | unknown message type | zod | Y | ignore + one `[data]` warn per type | nothing |
| advanceTo | clock paused | n/a | Y | no-op | frozen values |
| cost | unknown model | n/a | Y | `null`, partial-sum basis | "unknown" |
| 14b smoke | binary fails on one OS | job failure | Y | no upload for that OS, `report` job prefix | "Incomplete" release note |
| 14b checksums | asset missing | gh error | Y | job not run until all 4 exist | prefix stays |
No catch-alls planned; every rescue logs one line with root/file/path context. GAPS: 0.

### Section 3: Security and threat model

| Threat | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cross-origin page opens WS | Med | High (prompts, paths) | Y: Origin 403, token via hello |
| DNS rebinding | Low | High | Y: Host gate 421 under dev, preview, binary |
| Non-localhost network client | Low | High | Y: binds 127.0.0.1 (binary, preview), `localhost` (dev) |
| `/api/session` token read cross-origin | Low | Med | Y: no CORS, Sec-Fetch-Site, Host gate |
| Local process reads token | Med | Low | Accepted: it can read the logs directly (README) |
| Path traversal via cursor `path` | Med | High | finding → client cursors are matched against the server's known-file set; unknown paths ignored (added to accepted block) |
| Log content to browser | n/a in 14 | High in 15 | 14 sends counts and root paths only; D16 redaction test in 15 |
| New deps (`ws`) | Low | Med | pinned by lockfile; UC1 decides release of fixes |
| Release attestation | Low | Med | attest-build-provenance SHA-pinned (C7 guard) |

### Section 4: Data flow and interaction edge cases

```
 file append → watch event | rescan → tail(cursor) → [partial line? hold] → total → wire `lines` → logLines slice → HUD row
   shadow: empty file → total 0; huge file (24 h) → read in 64 KiB chunks; truncated → re-read; rotated → new fileId;
           non-UTF-8 bytes → counted by \n only; duplicate after reconnect → absolute totals replace
```
Async ordering: invariant "a file's displayed total equals its line count at the newest cursor". Overlap A: watch event and rescan both read the same file. Schedule 1: event reads to offset 100, rescan sees size 100, no-op. Schedule 2: rescan reads first, event then reads 0 bytes. Mechanism: one serial read queue per file (accepted below); both orders give the same total. Overlap B: reconnect hello with old cursors while a new append lands: server answers with absolute totals after the resume read, so order does not matter. Test: controlled pause between the two reads per file.

| Interaction | Edge case | Handled | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Try the demo" | double click | Y | sets params once; second click no-op |
| open tab, server restart | stale token | Y | T1 refresh |
| tab hidden for hours | many changes | Y | absolute totals on next message |
| zero roots / zero files | empty | Y | D9 card |
| 10k files in root | large list | Y | progress n/N, per-file totals |
Finding: per-file serial read queue and cursor path validation were missing; added.

### Section 5: Code quality

Fits existing patterns: pure modules with injected clocks (`clock.ts`), Host gate as a pure function. Risk of duplicate gate logic between `server.ts` and `plugin.ts`: one `logServer.ts` used by both (accepted in the architecture). `advanceTo` could branch more than 5 times (idle-end, lag, buckets, eviction); split into four pure helpers called in order. No over-engineering beyond T3/T4 taste items.

2am-Friday test: the restart integration test plus the logserver e2e. Hostile QA: rotate a file while the server is down and send a forged cursor path (now covered). Chaos: kill the server mid-backfill. Flakiness: watcher timing tests use the rescan path with a fake timer where possible; the 1 s e2e budget allows one retry. No LLM prompt changes.

### Section 7: Performance

Max sizes: buckets 60 per active session; tombstones 100,000 ids (about 4 MB [estimated]); `logLines` one entry per file in 24 h. `applyBatch` map copying (`reduce.ts:210`) bounded by X1. Slow paths: 24 h backfill read (streamed in 64 KiB chunks, progress per file), initial stat walk of large roots, Linux recursive watch setup. No DB.

### Section 8: Observability

`[logs]` lines at start, per root change, per rescan fallback; `[data]` lines for source status transitions and unknown wire types; HUD Data section shows status, per-file totals and metrics with basis; the pill tooltip carries the last error reason. Debuggable 3 weeks later from the terminal `[logs]` lines plus the HUD. Runbook rows added to CONTRIBUTING with 14b: "Incomplete" release prefix → re-run failed job.

### Section 9: Deployment and rollout

Three PRs in order 13, 14, 14b (13 and 14 can run in parallel; 14b after 14, or after 15 if UC2 changes it). No migrations. Rollback: revert PR (patch release). 14b risk window: first matrix run on a real `feat:` merge; mitigation: `workflow_dispatch` dry run of the matrix on the PR branch tag-less (builds and smokes without upload) before merge. Post-deploy: download the four assets, `gh attestation verify`, run the Mac binary.

Reversibility 4/5 (T2 watcher swap and T1 endpoint are local; Metric type is a one-way door for every later chunk, intended). Debt: `logLines` slice is temporary until chunk 15 (record in TODOS trigger). Platform potential: `wire.ts` and `Source` make OTLP ingest (F2) a second source later. Retrospective: X2 and X5 are load-bearing for tests and 14b smoke; good picks.

What exists: `sidecar/server.ts:80` `createServer` (node:http, Host gate, manifest assets), `sidecar/cli.ts:127` `run` (flags, port retry), `src/app/store/data.ts:80` `createDataSlice` (connect/ingest/sticky error at `setStatus`: `if (current.status === "error" || current.status === status) return;`), `src/data/reduce.ts:69` `DataState` (projects/sessions/subagents maps, ring with `seen` set), `src/data/mock.ts:444` `tick` (250 ms ticks via injected `schedule`). Auto-decided under /autoplan (P2 never reduce, P5 explicit): feature list kept; structure `Original arrangement` (one pure, tested module per concern: `sidecar/roots.ts`, `watch.ts`, `tail.ts`, `logServer.ts`, `plugin.ts`; `src/data/wire.ts`, `liveSource.ts`, `metrics.ts`, `jobs.ts`; `src/config/estimation.ts`, `prices.ts`) over a smaller merged `sidecar/logs.ts`, matching the repo's file-arrangement rule (PLAN chunk 06-10 "pure, unit-tested modules each get their own file"). C. Findings (eng, primary review):

- [P1] (confidence: 9/10) `src/app/store/data.ts` setStatus — `if (current.status === "error" || current.status === status) return;` makes `error` sticky until `connect`. If a dropped socket were reported as `error`, the live source could never return to `live`. Remedy E50: server-down and socket drops are `reconnecting`, never `error`; `error` is reserved for a second token rejection, invalid config (DX H4) and wire-schema failures. Accepted (P1, required for C72).
- [P1] (confidence: 9/10) `src/data/schema.ts` `Source` has only `onEvents`/`onStatus`; spec 1.3 asks every source to call `advanceTo`. Remedy E51: the store owns the cadence: it calls `advanceTo(clock.now())` after every ingest and from one store-owned 1 s real-time interval created in `connect` and cleared in `disconnect`; the `Source` interface does not change. Supersedes spec 1.3's "every source calls". Accepted (P5).
- [P1] (confidence: 8/10) Vite dev and preview share their HTTP server's `upgrade` event with Vite's own HMR WebSocket. Remedy E52: the log server handles upgrades only for its own path `/api/stream` and returns without touching the socket for any other path; Host/Origin gates apply only to the plugin's own routes (`/api/stream`, `/api/session`, `/api/import`, and the index templating), never to Vite's static or HMR traffic. Test: an HMR-path upgrade is left alone; a dev page still hot-reloads with the plugin installed. Accepted (P1).
- [P1] (confidence: 8/10) `transformIndexHtml` does not run under `vp preview` (static `dist/`). Remedy E53: under preview the plugin's `configurePreviewServer` registers a pre-middleware that templates `index.html` for `/`, `/index.html` and the SPA fallback (pass-2 3.5); dev uses `transformIndexHtml`; the binary templates in `sidecar/server.ts`. One `templateIndex(html, { token, mode })` helper serves all three. Accepted (P1, DRY).
- [P1] (confidence: 8/10) CEO Section 9 adds `workflow_dispatch` to the matrix, but `release.yml` runs semantic-release; a dispatch there would attempt a release. Remedy E54: the build/smoke/attest/upload matrix lives in a reusable workflow `.github/workflows/binaries.yml` (`workflow_call` with inputs `version`, `ref`, `upload`; `workflow_dispatch` with `upload: false`), called by `release.yml` after `release` with `upload: true`; `binaries.yml` opens with `permissions: {}` and job-level grants (C7 guard). Test: `release-workflow.test.ts` asserts the call, inputs and that dispatch never uploads. Accepted (P5).
- [P2] (confidence: 8/10) X1 eviction needs to know when a session is no longer in the ring. Remedy E55: the ring keeps a per-session reference count updated on push and overwrite; eviction runs inside `advanceTo` for `done` sessions with count 0. Accepted.
- [P2] (confidence: 8/10) Adding `todo`/`toolClass` to mock events would change the chunk 12 steady digests (E36, byte-identical contract). Remedy E56: the mock stays unchanged in chunk 13; job-stage tests use hand-written fixture events in `src/data/jobs.test.ts`. Accepted (protects an approved contract).
- [P2] (confidence: 7/10) The trailing tokens/min window slides every sim second even without events, so "integrate exactly across every input change" means per-second steps. Remedy E57: `advanceTo` integrates the lag per one-second step while any bucket in the 60 s window is non-zero and uses the closed-form decay once the window is empty, so a 10-minute hidden tab at 60x costs at most 60 steps per session. Accepted.
- [P2] (confidence: 7/10) Backfill of many files at server start could block the event loop. Remedy E58: backfill reads with streams in 64 KiB chunks, at most 4 files concurrently, newest mtime first, yielding between chunks; progress counts files. Test: 500 fixture files backfill without one read over 64 KiB. Accepted.
